newsitem.title: JAPAN: Drug spending cut may pressure Japan firms-Moody"s.
newsitem.headline: Drug spending cut may pressure Japan firms-Moody"s.

text.p: Moody"s Investors Service said on Monday that the Japanese government"s plans to cut drug spending are likely to have a negative impact on the credit quality of weaker pharmaceutical firms.
However, stronger drug firms will be supported over the medium term by the steady launch of new products and expansion in international operations, Moody"s said in a statement.

"The Japanese government plans to contain the country"s burgeoning health care bills through drastic reductions in drug expenditures are likely to have a negative impact on the credit quality of Japan"s weaker pharmaceutical companies," it said.

It said, however, that of the nine pharmaceutical makers it has rated, Takeda Chemical Industries Ltd and Sankyo Co Ltd are best positioned to deal successfully with the forthcoming changes in the pharmaceuticals industry.
The two firms and Eisai Co Ltd should benefit from strong upcoming products and sound financial fundamentals, Moody"s said.
"Only those companies that successfully undertake the steady launch of new products and direct their resources outside Japan will remain competitive," Moody"s said.
If domestic drug sales proved insufficient to pay for research and development costs, some weaker companies may not survive or may be merged with stronger players, Moody"s said.

Moody"s currently rates nine Japanese pharmaceuticals companies. They are: Chugai Pharmaceutical Co Ltd (rated A3), Daiichi Pharmaceutical Co Ltd (A1), Eisai (A1), Fujisawa Pharmaceutical Co Ltd (A3), Sankyo (Aa3), Shionogi and Co Ltd (A2), Takeda (P-1), Tanabe Seiyaku Co Ltd (A3) and Yamanouchi Pharmaceutical Co Ltd (Aa3).
